newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Aalberts seeks wider markets.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Aalberts seeks wider markets.

text.p: Dutch industrial holding company Aalberts Industries said on Thursday it would continue to strengthen its position in Europe over the next couple of years, but would also pursue further globalisation.

"European development remains our number one priority," company president Jan Aalberts told reporters, adding: "The share of our activities outside Europe is still too small, but we remain careful with our strategy."
"An essential part of our products has the potential to be sold worldwide," he said, noting good growth possibilities in Eastern Europe.
Aalberts said the company intended to take a majority stake in a small Polish production firm, adding the number of products Aalberts currently exports to Poland would rise.
Together with a local partner, Aalberts had 1996 turnover of more than $1 million in the United States making heating valves.
"We expect very nice growth in the U.S., particularly in this field," Aalberts said, adding that it also intended to grow in South America. "There are some possibilities there."
Aalberts said he expected 20-25 percent of the company's business to be generated outside Europe within the next five years or so, adding that much depended on how markets developed.
All three divisions had clear growth potential, he said.
"We are looking for organic growth, and for acquisitions when they make sense."

Aalberts, which makes and sells installation materials, dispensing systems and special components, had 1996 turnover of 471 million guilders, of which 156 million was generated in the Netherlands and 163 million in Germany.
1996 net profit was 26.2 million guilders, a 30 percent increase on the previous year.
The company said earlier that, barring unforeseen circumstances, it expected further growth in turnover, operating result, net profit and earnings per share in 1997.
